content.text:
Send this from the **Chain** tab. It changes both the spec and the code.

```
Every run of the harness should start with what it needs to work on a Piton
project, and a small, predictable context rather than an old transcript.

1. Piton fluency in every mode. @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} gains a third
placeholder, PITON_FLUENCY, alongside CODE_LOCATION and SPEC_LOCATION. It
stands for the output of `piton claude --print-prompt`, run in the project
directory. It is run once when the project is opened and kept for as long as
it stays open. Where `piton` isn't installed or fails, it is replaced with
nothing, and the run goes ahead without it. Every mode's default template
(Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask) ends with PITON_FLUENCY, and like the other
placeholders it can be moved or removed in @{SettingsWindowScope}. Projects
whose saved templates predate it keep them as they are.

2. Following references. Every mode's default template also says: "Links to
.claude/reference/… in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each
one before changing anything it covers."

3. Starting a new conversation. Tasks and questions each carry on their own
conversation, as @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says. Add a "New conversation"
button to @{ChatInputScope}, at the right end of the help text beside the
tabs, that starts a new conversation for the selected tab: tasks for Code,
Chain, and Spec, questions for Ask. The next run in that tab starts fresh
instead of carrying on. Its tooltip says which conversation it resets. It is
disabled while that conversation has nothing to carry on, and while a run in
it is under way. The choice survives reopening the project, so a project
opened after its conversation was reset starts fresh too, rather than
carrying on the latest conversation in its history.
```

**What I did with your attachment**
- I left out the "Code:" part (the `src/ribbon/mod.rs` and `src/main_window.rs` notes). It reads like the summary of an earlier ribbon task, not something to request. If you meant it as a change, send it separately in Code mode.
- I kept the fluency prompt and the link-following line as your text had them, and added what an agent would otherwise have to guess: what happens when `piton` is missing, and that existing saved templates are left alone.
- **"New conversation" placement:** I put it in the chat input so it resets the tab you're on. The ribbon's Code tab would also work, if you'd rather keep the input bar clean.
- **Persistence:** the prompt makes a reset last across reopening the project. Without that, the app would find the old session id in the history and resume it again, as it does now.

Two things you may want to add as a line each:
- **Context size:** "Beside the button, the size of the conversation the next run will carry on, in tokens, from the latest run's report."
- **Automatic reset:** "A conversation is started fresh automatically once it passes 200k tokens."
